---
title: "Recreativity"
description: "Use play, creativity, curiosity, and novelty to widen behavioral options."
---

::: {.tsk-page-lede}
Recreativity means deliberately making room for play, curiosity, making, and low-stakes experimentation. It can be useful when life has narrowed into only coping, productivity, or problem solving.
:::

## Creative reset {#creative-reset}

Set a timer for five to fifteen minutes and make something with no requirement that it be good or useful.

Possible prompts:

- sketch the room without erasing,
- make a tiny collage from scraps,
- write six strange lines,
- photograph five interesting textures,
- rearrange a shelf only for visual interest,
- improvise a snack from what is already available.

The objective is behavioral flexibility, not artistic achievement.

## Play window {#play-window}

Reserve a short block of time for an activity chosen because it is absorbing, funny, satisfying, or curious.

A play window works best when it has a boundary. Ten minutes of a puzzle can restore attention; an undefined evening of avoidance may create a different problem.

Ask: **What activity gives me a different mode of attention without creating a large cost afterward?**

## Novelty dose {#novelty}

Introduce one small new element into a familiar routine:

- take a different walking route,
- cook one unfamiliar ingredient,
- listen to a new genre,
- work from a different chair,
- visit a library section you normally ignore,
- learn a tiny manual skill.

Novelty can be especially useful when days feel repetitive or emotionally flat. Keep the dose small enough that it feels interesting rather than overwhelming.

## Recreate before you evaluate

When motivation is low, waiting to feel interested before doing anything can keep the system narrow. Try a brief activity first, then evaluate whether it changed energy, attention, or mood at all.

::: {.tsk-note}
Recreation is not a reward that must be earned by perfect productivity. It is one of the ways people restore capacity, connection, and flexibility.
:::
